scientific_question: Do donors with worse memory decline show a greater burden of hypertrophic lymphocyte-contacting reactive astrocytes in the CA1 pyramidal niche, beyond the current panel's separate count-based astrocyte and immune-contact features?
rationale: Rounds 4 and 7 showed that peripyramidal reactive astrocyte size and lymphocyte contact each add signal, but rounds 8-9 suggest simple binary lymphocyte-presence features are nearing redundancy. The right next test is a cleaner combined biomarker that asks whether the true residual signal is specifically the area-weighted burden of immune-associated reactive astrocytes around CA1 pyramidal neurons, which could either add a sharper severity axis or replace a weaker count-only immune feature.
approach: Assign cells to CA1 by centroid using CustomAnnotations polygons after dividing annotation coordinates by 16. Identify CA1 Pyramidal Neuron, Reactive Astrocyte, and Lymphocyte cells from ClassificationNode labels. Compute reactive astrocyte contour area in um^2 after centering contours, then converting pixel area using slide MPP. Define a reactive astrocyte as peripyramidal if its centroid is within 30 um of any CA1 pyramidal neuron centroid. For each peripyramidal reactive astrocyte, mark whether it has at least one CA1 lymphocyte within a lymphocyte-contact radius X. The donor-level biomarker is sum(area_um2 of lymphocyte-contacting peripyramidal reactive astrocytes) divided by count(all peripyramidal reactive astrocytes), yielding an area-weighted immune-contact burden with score 0 when contact is absent but the niche exists.

variations.name: candidate_variant_a
variations.description: Baseline: peripyramidal reactive astrocytes are within 30 um of a CA1 pyramidal neuron, lymphocyte contact defined as at least 1 CA1 lymphocyte within 20 um, donor score = summed contact-positive reactive astrocyte area / peripyramidal reactive astrocyte count.

variations.name: candidate_variant_b
variations.description: Nearby local change: keep the same 30 um peripyramidal definition and burden formula, but expand the lymphocyte-contact radius from 20 um to 25 um.

notes: Use centroid-to-centroid distances with a spatial index for speed. Keep all cell populations restricted to CA1 for regional specificity. If a donor has no peripyramidal reactive astrocytes, return NaN; if peripyramidal reactive astrocytes exist but none contact lymphocytes, return 0. Read slide MPP from the paired SVS if convenient; the cohort MPP range is narrow, but area conversion should be consistent across donors.
prompt_text:
# Candidate Proposer

You are proposing exactly one candidate biomarker round for an iterative
autoresearch loop.

This system is deliberately simple:

- there is one accepted biomarker panel so far
- each round proposes one new candidate biomarker family
- the worker may test a small local sweep within that candidate family
- the evaluator compares:
  - current accepted panel score
  - panel + candidate score
  - panel with one member replaced by the candidate
- the system then keeps the best reviewed panel only if it improves the train panel score

Your job is only to propose the next candidate.

You will receive a JSON payload containing:

- `program`: the research directive
- `data_summary`: dataset guide
- `accepted_panel`: the current accepted biomarker panel
- `recent_results`: recent keep/discard history from results.tsv
- `round_id`
- `candidate_type`: `seed` if the panel is empty, otherwise `candidate`

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "short stable slug",
  "scientific_question": "one sentence stating the candidate hypothesis",
  "rationale": "why this candidate is the right next test based on recent results",
  "approach": "how to compute the biomarker from the data",
  "variations": [
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_a",
      "description": "baseline or central parameterization"
    },
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_b",
      "description": "one nearby local change"
    }
  ],
  "baseline_variation": "candidate_variant_a",
  "notes": "data access, coordinate, or implementation notes for the worker"
}
```

## Rules

- Propose exactly one candidate family per round.
- Keep the candidate biologically interpretable.
- If `candidate_type` is `seed`, propose the strongest plausible seed biomarker.
- If `candidate_type` is `candidate`, propose something that could improve the
  accepted panel either by adding new signal or by being a cleaner replacement
  for one weaker existing member.
- Prefer one local family sweep with 2-4 nearby variations, not a grab bag of
  unrelated ideas.
- Use recent results to avoid exact repetition.
- Make the local sweep explicit and small:
  - one radius change
  - one threshold change
  - one local operator change
  - or one biologically coherent gating change
- Do not talk about planners, branches, coordinators, or analyzers.
- Focus on one candidate that is easy to compute and easy to audit.

## Quality bar

A good proposal is:

- specific
- testable in one round
- mechanistically interpretable
- plausibly additive to the accepted panel
- not a vague restatement of the prior winner
